newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends firmer after range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends firmer after range-bound trade.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen interest rate futures contract traded in a tight range on Thursday and ended slightly firmer.

Those who had gone short in the morning covered their positions later because of a widespread view that there may not be a rate rise until the end of this year despite a sharp rise in machinery orders for May, traders said.
Japan's private sector machinery orders rose a seasonally adjusted 12.9 percent in May from the previous month.
Traders said the rise in orders failed to change the bullish tone because the data was within market expectations.

"Many operators paid little attention to the data because the market is currently biased upward," said a long-term credit bank dealer. The contract may rise above technical resistance at 99.02 if fresh economic data indicates that Japan's economic recovery may halt later this year, he said.
The March was up 0.02 at 99.02 after moving between 98.99 and 99.02. Turnover was 40,752 contracts.
The focus is on stocks as they are a clue to the strength of the economic recovery, traders said. The Nikkei-225 stock index ended up 57.61 points or 0.29 percent at 19,754.78.
"If the Nikkei falls below the key 19,500 level, the March contract may rise to 99.05," said a city bank dealer.
In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate was around 0.51 percent, against Wednesday's 0.50 percent.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) left neither a surplus nor a shortfall in the market by injecting 300 billion yen through its morning operation. It was the fourth straight day that the BOJ had conducted a neutral operation.
The long-end benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) rate eased to 0.66 percent from Wednesday's 0.67.

"Many banks hope there will be no rate rise this year. So they tend to think that the current rates are too high," said a city bank dealer. Traders said one city bank issued some 40 billion yen worth of the CDs at 0.66 percent after the CDs were issued at 0.67 percent in the morning.

In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, a few domestic banks bought fixed interest rates, but trade was lacklustre. The five-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.92/1.96 percent, down from Wednesday's 1.94/1.98. -- Risa Maeda +81-33432-8570
